title: Quality management and analytics
blurb: Evaluations, monitoring, analytics wording, and the claims this check would not upgrade.
summary: Quality scores a recording against a form. Analytics sweeps interactions. The percents stay on the page that printed them.

lessons.title: Quality management scores the work on purpose
objectives: Keep QM, surveys, and analytics apart
Do not invent the small-share percent
paragraphs: The workforce engagement page describes quality management as multi-channel evaluations, real-time agent desktop monitoring and assistance, and automated scoring and evaluation selection. The quality page says manual review covers a small share of interactions and frames that as a problem the product is aimed at. It does not give this lab a measured percent.

A score without a recording and a form is a mood. The WEM data-sheet page says the suite is about integrating recording with quality management, interaction analytics, workforce management, recording data protection, customer surveys, and CRM connectors. Those are the pieces. They are not one button.

lessons.title: Analytics is a sweep across interactions
objectives: Quote the percent with its page
paragraphs: The WEM page says interaction analytics analyzes 100 percent of captured interactions to find trends, automate the quality process, and see where service went well or badly. The feature list names voice, chat, and email, 100 percent call transcription, automated QM scoring, statistical group comparison, ad hoc word or phrase search, automatic categorization, and emotion and sentiment analysis.

The quality page's conversational-intelligence line says analyze up to 100 percent of interactions. Up to 100 percent and 100 percent are not the same sentence. Quote the page you mean. This lesson does not average them into a single guarantee.
uncertain: The WEM page says 100 percent of captured interactions and 100 percent call transcription. The quality page says up to 100 percent. This lesson does not merge them.

lessons.title: Performance views are dashboards, wallboards, and KPIs
objectives: Use the performance nouns the page printed
paragraphs: The WEM page lists performance management separately from quality and from analytics: role-based customizable dashboards, customizable KPIs and metrics, real-time performance visibility, data from external sources, wallboards, and gamification.

A wallboard is not a standard report, and gamification is not a disposition. The page names them. It does not define a formula for a KPI. The analytics PDF downloaded in this check did not yield readable sentences, so no retention month and no chart-count is taken from it.

lessons.title: Agents can read evaluations without a second story
objectives: Show the evaluation where the page says it can live
paragraphs: The desktop page says Plus can show schedules, adherence, time-off requests, and evaluations without leaving the desktop. The same page says WFO connectors can show schedules, adherence, time off, shift bidding, and evaluation review inside the CRM.

Recording on the WEM page is described as full-time capture of customer interactions and agent screens, kept in encrypted storage. That is the page's sentence. Notice and consent laws are not restated here, because this check did not re-open the license. Do not skip them. Confirm them on the license before you record.
uncertain: Notice and consent are not re-quoted in this chapter. The license page was not the source opened for these lessons.

paragraphs: Finish a quality note with the lists that opened. Name the form, the monitoring, the analytics sentence with its percent attached to a page, and the place the agent reads the score. Say whether you mean the WEM list or the quality page when the words differ.

The quality page also says routing, assistance, and coaching can be refined with zero human involvement. That is the page's claim. This lab did not run that cycle. Treat it as a product sentence, not as a result you measured.
